subject: Study Skills
title: Lecture 5 - Teamwork and Small Group Learning (Mixed Bank)

A.q: Which description fits a small group?
A.explain: A small group has eight to twelve learners, is teacher-facilitated and learner-centered, and uses free discussion.
Teamwork is effective cooperation and communication with others toward a common goal. The other options describe a team, small-group skills, or mere placement.

A.q: Which statement about teams and groups is correct?
options: A group counts as a team.
Not every group forms a team.
A.explain: A team is a group of individuals, but a group becomes a team only when members cooperate toward a shared goal.

A.q: Which sequence shows the stages of team development?
A.explain: Team development proceeds from Forming to Storming, then Norming, then Performing.

A.q: Which stage has questions, structure, roles, trust, guidelines, and a directive tutor?
A.explain: Forming involves questions, clear structure, goals, roles, trust-building, guideline setting, and a directive tutor.

A.q: Which stage has frustration, disagreements, refocusing, conflict skills, and a directive tutor?
A.explain: Storming involves frustration, less polite disagreements, refocusing on goals, conflict-management skills, and a directive tutor.

A.q: Which stage has meaningful communication, ground rules, evaluation, productivity, and a participative tutor?
A.explain: Norming includes meaningful communication, return to ground rules, process evaluation, higher productivity, and a participative tutor.

A.q: Which stage has can-do attitude, helping behaviors, fluid roles, appreciated differences, and celebrated progress?
A.explain: Performing shows a can-do attitude, offers to help, fluid roles, appreciated differences, significant progress, and celebrated accomplishments.

A.q: Sort each example into its correct category.
A.explain: Punctuality is a ground rule, active involvement is a value of small groups, clinical rounds are a form, and mutual respect is a team characteristic.

A.q: Match each team-development stage to its main feeling.

rightItems.text: Frustration or anger about progress or process.
Excitement, eagerness, high expectations, and some anxiety.
Satisfaction and attachment beyond the sum of parts.
Acceptance of others; constructive criticism is welcome.

A.explain: Forming brings excitement and anxiety, Storming brings frustration, Norming brings acceptance, and Performing brings satisfaction and attachment.
A team is a group of people working cooperatively to achieve a common goal.

A.q: Why are teams useful for complex tasks?
options: They remove the need for shared goals.
A.explain: Teams share goals, commitment, and skills to complete complex tasks beyond individual capacity.

options: Teams remove the need for roles.
A.explain: Teams are part of everyone's life, so students need to function effectively as team members.

A.q: Which set contains only sample ground rules?
options: On time, prepared, listening, shared responsibility.
Common purpose, prepared, listening, shared responsibility.
On time, field training, listening, shared responsibility.
On time, prepared, listening, measurable goals.
A.explain: Sample ground rules are punctuality, preparation, listening and understanding, and shared responsibility for group aims.

A.q: Which set contains only reasons that small-group learning is valuable?
A.explain: Small-group learning develops positive attitudes, problem-solving and decision-making skills, and active involvement.

A.q: Which set contains only forms of small-group learning?
options: Ground rules, field training, rounds, projects.
PBL, field training, rounds, measurable goals.
A.explain: Small groups are used in PBL classes, field training, clinical rounds, and research projects; PBL means Problem Based Learning.

A.q: Which set contains only characteristics of a successful team?
A.explain: Successful teams have common purpose, measurable goals, effective leadership, and mutual respect.
